subject: RSW_Excretor

reply.subject: RSW_Excretor

observed.facings.png: Three facings at one shared scale on a checkerboard. Heavy, barrel-bodied four-legged grazer with slate-blue-grey wrinkled skin, a back covered in overlapping mineral plates crusted with pale salt and streaked with rust-orange and verdigris, a row of glossy amber pods along each flank, thick pillar legs with split pale hooves, and a short tail ending in a crusted tuft. South: head-on front with a plated face, small orange eyes, two curved dark outer horns and a straight pale central brow horn. East: side profile, head lowered and facing right, outer horns curving up with the central horn rising between them, amber pods in a row along the flank. North: rear view showing the haunches, the tail with its crusted tip, the plated back, and three horn tips above the back. No face shows on the north view.
observed.south.png: The front view at full resolution. The face looks at the camera, with a pale crusted face plate, orange eyes, a broad muzzle, two curved horns sweeping out and up, and one straight conical brow horn in the middle. The plated, salt-crusted back rises behind the head, and amber gland pods show on both shoulders and flanks. Four legs with split hooves. Clean alpha.
observed.east.png: A true side profile facing right. A long, deep body with a sagging belly, plates and white mineral crust along the spine, a row of about six amber, egg-like pods along the flank with granular crust inside, and a tail with an orange-crusted tuft. The head is low, with one large curved outer horn and two straighter horns showing above the face. Clean alpha, no ground.
observed.north.png: The rear view: rounded haunches, the tail hanging down the middle with a crusted tuft, the plated back seen from behind, amber pods on both flanks, and the hind hooves. Three horn tips (two curved outer, one straight central) show above the back. No eyes or face. Clean alpha.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the creature is about 2 cells long and about 1.6 cells tall, clearly larger than the human. At normal play (32 px per cell) it reads as a grey bulk with a pale crusted back, an orange band along the flank and horns at the right end, distinct from the ground.

SOUTH_FRONT.seen: South is the head-on front: face, eyes and muzzle toward the camera.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North shows the haunches, the tail and the plated back. Only the horn tips show above the back, with no face or eyes.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: All three facings use the angled game camera, not a top-down view.

SAME_SIZE.seen: The measured height spread is 12%, within 15%. The facings look consistent on the shared-scale panel.

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: Hide, plates, amber pods, tail tuft and horn set match on every facing. The horns turn with the head: a fan seen from the front on south, layered along the head on east, tips above the back on north.

SIGNATURE.seen: Three horns and mineral-concentrating glands are clearly legible: amber pods along the flanks and salt crust over the plates.

ALIEN.seen: The body plan is rhino-like, but the mineral-plated, crusted back, the rows of glowing amber flank pods and the three-horn crown make it read as an alien grazer, not a recoloured rhino or bison.

DEPARTURES.seen: (1) Mineral-plated slate hide with no fur: present on all facings. (2) Three horns, two curved outer horns and one straight central brow horn: present on south, east and north. (3) Salt-crusted gland nodules along the flanks: present as rows of amber pods with granular crust inside, flanked by white salt crust on the plates.

CANON.seen: Three horns show in every facing. It does not read as a feral nerf or bison reskin: there is no fur or hump, and it has plates and pods.

STYLE.seen: Painterly, with detailed texture and a clean outline. Not cel-shaded or cute; the eyes are small and not glossy.

OURS.seen: Original art that matches the description. Not vanilla Muffalo, Bison or Thrumbo art.

ALPHA.seen: Real alpha on all facings, with no ground patch, shadow or backdrop.

OWNER_NOTES.seen: N and S both show three horns. The new drawing is more alien than the nerf, with plates, crust and glands.

SCALE.seen: About 2 cells long and clearly bigger than the human, which fits 'heavy-set' and drawSize 2.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px it reads as a grey body with a pale back, an orange flank band and horns.

findings.seen: In profile the low-slung head, wrinkled grey skin and pillar legs read quite rhinoceros-like. The plates and pods carry the alien identity.
findings.quote: Invented creatures and plants read as ALIEN, never as a recoloured Earth species.
findings.fix: The head shows a more unfamiliar profile, such as a plated, beak-like muzzle or crusted mineral ridges along the jaw, so the side view reads as a non-Earth grazer.

proposals: The amber flank pods could show a small dense layered pellet at one or two sites, to tie the art to the 'sheds pellets' behaviour.

reply.subject: RSW_Excretor
reply.image_seen: The panels show a heavy grey quadruped with overlapping slate plates, pale mineral crusts, orange flank nodules and three horns, viewed from front, side and rear, plus a human scale comparison.

concerns.evidence: The east view has rhinoceros-like proportions, but its overlapping slate armour, raised mineral-encrusted back plates and orange flank gland nodules visibly establish the required alien departures. Two curved outer horns and a straight central horn are visible in all three facings. Earth-animal resemblance alone does not meet the stated failure condition when these departures are present.
